claim: A standalone native macOS broker can issue signed, path-free file capabilities and an OS-sandboxed consumer can prepare the approved snapshots while being denied access to an unrelated local file.
limitations: The isolation proof used a synthetic signed fixture; the participant has not yet completed the native app flow recorded in public evidence.
The local app is ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed or notarised.
The compiled consumer uses deprecated macOS sandbox-exec for measurable POC isolation.
A production client should use a separately signed App Sandbox helper or XPC service.
No real personal data was read or trained on; the opt-in fixture used synthetic email-like identifiers.
Everything-compatible currently means recursive UTF-8 Markdown, text and common image files, not email databases, PDFs, office documents, audio or video.
Image inputs produce private OCR, broad-label and face-count text for language-model training; no visual-model fine-tuning is claimed.
No accessibility, localisation, leakage, revocation, deletion or independent security review is claimed.
No model training or multi-computer round occurred in Gate 1c itself.
